end.summary:
Discussed the East India Company’s shift from trade to political control.
Reviewed Plassey (1757), Buxar (1764), Diwani rights (1765), and Crown rule after 1857.
Covered revenue collection, armies, forts, artisans, machine-made cloth, cash crops, indigo, and famines.
The order of Buxar and Diwani was mixed up initially, then corrected in later responses.
Teach-back was not completed successfully.
end.parentNote: Asha practised how the Company moved from trading to ruling through forts, armies, battles, and revenue collection. Zoya explained the effects on artisans, cloth production, cash crops, and famines. They first mixed up the sequence of Buxar and Diwani, but corrected it later by stating Buxar came in 1764 and Diwani in 1765. At home, ask them to make a four-step timeline: Charter, Plassey, Buxar, and Diwani, then add Crown rule after 1857.
